Looking at the decision index benchmarks and wow pervasive overfitting of models!!! 

I'm more likely to use a model that has a high & consistent public + private score vs. those with a huge drift

Also, beware - the models are sorted by public scores in the individual benchmark cards

I’m glad that more people are scrutinizing popular AI benchmarks.  

Eugene did a deep dive into 12 benchmarks and writes about the surprising things he found like:

1. Erroneous graders 
2. Misconfigured harnesses 
3. Unrealistic specifications that don’t resemble how people use AI 
4. Problems with environments 

He also makes a good arguments about cost per task and metrics that have been Goodhart-nerfed 

Highly recommended reading!

I don’t really care about how many PRs you merged with AI, I want to hear about how you are making exponentially more money with AI

Love to see error bars on benchmarks 

It’s very much a chart crime not to show them

The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is currently made up of 9 benchmarks with arbitrary weights.  

I wanted to know how these weights varied over time.  They vary quite a bit!

This comment illustrates the Evals-Industrial complex 

1. [The belief that] If you can’t convince people to benchmaxx on your benchmark it is “worthless”

2. If people do infact benchmaxx on them they statistically become worthless 

cc: @xeophon

I see some are drawing the wrong inference from this study: they are focusing on this meta benchmark as yet another benchmark for model picking, i.e. open vs closed models, model families etc.  

That’s too narrow of an interpretation!  You need to do your own private evals on your specific tasks to know what’s “better”

This should give you healthy skepticism of all public benchmarks.  I believe that was the intention of this illustration to begin with.
The industrial-benchmark complex is on thin ice
